title: No-parameter lambdas: a lazy fallback and a factory of fresh lists

blocks.text: A lambda with no parameters must still be written with empty parentheses: `() -> ...`. As a `Supplier`, it holds work back until someone calls `get()`, and its body runs again on every call.

items: `valueOr(String value, Supplier<String> fallback)` returns `value` when it is not `null`, and otherwise the result of a fresh `fallback.get()` call, made every time the fallback is needed and never remembered between calls.
`freshLists()` returns a `Supplier<List<String>>` whose `get()` gives an empty, modifiable list.

blocks.text: A fallback may be costly to compute, and several callers may share one list factory.

cases.says: It returns the value when there is one and the fallback's result when the value is null.
The factory's list starts empty and accepts new elements.
The fallback supplier is not called at all when the value is present.
Each get() returns a new list; filling one leaves the next empty.

concepts: A no-parameter lambda holds its work back until it is called, and runs its body again on every call.
